page.title: Self-hosted subscription trackers, compared
page.lede: Five open-source subscription trackers run well on your own server: Wallos, SubTrackr, Renewlet, Zublo and Coinio. All five ship as a Docker container that keeps its data in SQLite. They differ most in license, notification channels, AI features and how many people can sign in.
page.checked: Every claim comes from each project's README or website, checked on 20 November 2026. Star counts are rounded. We make Coinio, so read its entry with that in mind.
list.name: Open-source self-hosted subscription trackers
list.title: The five trackers, one by one
list.lede: What each project is built with, its license, the feature that sets it apart and the kind of person it suits.
wallos.stack: PHP 8.3 and SQLite; Docker or bare metal
wallos.standout: The broadest feature set: household members, OIDC sign-in, six notification channels, AI saving tips and 21+ languages.
wallos.best: Households, and anyone who wants the most established option.
subtrackr.stack: Go (Gin), HTMX, Tailwind CSS and SQLite
subtrackr.standout: Calendar export to iCal with a subscription URL, To Cancel reminders before a cancellation deadline, and an MCP server.
subtrackr.best: People who want renewals in their own calendar app and push alerts through ntfy, Gotify or Pushover.
renewlet.stack: React, Go and PocketBase with SQLite; or Cloudflare Workers with D1
renewlet.standout: Ten notification channels, AI that turns screenshots or tables into drafts, budgets, and a shareable public status page.
renewlet.best: People who want many reminder channels (WeCom, DingTalk and Bark among them), budgets, or a serverless deploy on Cloudflare.
zublo.stack: React, Vite and PocketBase with SQLite
zublo.standout: An AI layer with chat and recommendations over Gemini, OpenAI, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, plus TOTP two-factor sign-in.
zublo.best: People who want to chat with their spending data, and developers who like PocketBase.
coinio.standout: Family & shared splits, passkeys, built-in MCP with OAuth, Firefly III sync, free cloud at app.getcoinio.me, iPhone/Android ScriptWidget, 9 alert channels and custom CSS/HTML.
coinio.best: Individuals and families splitting shared plans who want passkeys, AI assistants and an iPhone widget, plus Wallos users looking for something lighter (imports Wallos Paid By too).

choose.title: How to choose
choose.lede: Start with two questions: who will use it, and where do you want to be reminded? Most of the choice follows from the answers.
choose.users.q: Several people, each with a login?
choose.users.a: Wallos supports independent multi-user logins, household members and OIDC sign-in. Zublo also has multiple users. SubTrackr's login is optional. Coinio supports family & shared households with member profiles, single-use invite links, private personal bills and passkey sign-in.
choose.notify.a: Renewlet has the most built-in channels, including WeCom, DingTalk and Bark. Wallos and SubTrackr both cover email, Pushover, Gotify and webhooks, Wallos adds Discord and Telegram, and SubTrackr adds ntfy. Coinio covers email, Telegram, Discord, Slack, ntfy, Gotify, Pushover and webhooks, and reaches 100+ more services through Apprise.
choose.ai.q: Want to talk to an AI assistant?
choose.ai.a: Coinio and SubTrackr ship MCP servers. Coinio's runs over https with OAuth, so claude.ai and ChatGPT can connect from anywhere; SubTrackr's is a binary that a local MCP client starts. Wallos and Zublo use AI for saving tips and chat, Renewlet for turning screenshots into entries.
choose.calendar.a: SubTrackr exports iCal and offers a subscription URL. Renewlet can add all or single subscriptions to a calendar. The others show a calendar inside the app.
choose.license.q: Does the license matter to you?
choose.license.a: Renewlet and Coinio use MIT, Zublo uses Apache-2.0, Wallos GPL-3.0 and SubTrackr AGPL-3.0. For personal use all of them are free; the difference shows when you modify the code and share it or host it for others.
choose.wallos.a: Renewlet and Coinio both import Wallos data, so you can try either without retyping everything. For a closer look, read the Coinio and Wallos comparison.
pfaq.title: Common questions
pfaq.best.q: What is the best self-hosted subscription tracker?
pfaq.best.a: There is no single best one. Wallos is the most established and supports OIDC. Renewlet ships ten notification channels, SubTrackr suits calendar-driven reminders, Zublo leans on AI chat, and Coinio suits individuals and families splitting shared plans who want passkeys, AI assistants and an iPhone widget.
pfaq.free.a: Yes. All five are open source and free to self-host. Their licenses differ: MIT (Renewlet, Coinio), Apache-2.0 (Zublo), GPL-3.0 (Wallos) and AGPL-3.0 (SubTrackr).
pfaq.database.q: Do I need a separate database server?
pfaq.database.a: No. All five keep their data in SQLite, so one container and a data folder are enough. Renewlet can also run on Cloudflare Workers with D1 instead.
pfaq.ai.q: Which ones work with Claude or ChatGPT?
pfaq.ai.a: Coinio and SubTrackr include MCP servers. Coinio's is served over https with OAuth, so claude.ai and ChatGPT can connect to it remotely. SubTrackr's runs as a binary that local MCP clients start, for example through docker exec.
pfaq.checked.a: We read each project's README and website on 20 November 2026 and took star counts from GitHub the same day. These projects move fast, so check the linked repositories before you decide. Spotted a mistake? Open an issue.
final.title: Want to try Coinio?
final.lede: It installs with one command, and the live demo runs right in your browser.
